prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1144; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Rear-end collision reported by the policyholder's household member, who was driving the insured vehicle at the time. The claimant is represented by counsel, and the file has been opened for bodily injury and property damage.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene show the rear damage on the claimant's vehicle and a matching impact area on the insured vehicle. Police and two bystanders confirm the claimant was in the vehicle when the collision happened. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision occurred.

Entry 3: The claimant reports neck and back strain, and the reported injury fits the type and force of a rear impact. Medical records show no prior treatment to the same body areas, and no earlier injury has been identified through the claims database.

Entry 4: Counsel has provided a treatment summary. Visits and new services have been added steadily over several months, which is well beyond what this type of strain usually requires. The adjuster has requested the treatment plan and the referral basis for each new service.

Entry 5: The claimant's account of the collision has stayed the same in every conversation, including the initial report, the recorded statement, and the follow-up call with counsel present. The estimate for the rear damage is largely consistent with the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle has been found.

Entry 6: The policy was in force on the date of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start. The driver lives with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member. The file is being held for review of the treatment records before any settlement position is set.
